title: Adaptive compile matrix for sharded expert + grouped-attention models
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Goal: Produce an adaptive compile matrix and publishing workflow that ensures sharded MoE and grouped-attention (GQA) models receive deterministic, validated kernel selections and compilation tuning that meet performance SLOs across GPU families. This ticket covers: compile-key design, per-model manifest fields for pinning, CI/validation harness changes, rollout playbook (canary + rollback), and docs for model on-boarders in Research/Applied ML and Solutions Engineering.
acceptance_criteria: Compile matrix format documented and added to model manifest schema (fields: kernel_variant, compile_flags_hash, hw_tags, seq_len_profile)
Automated compile cache keys produced deterministically for sharded-MoE and GQA variants
Validation harness produces P50/P95 latency and tokens/sec baseline for every profile and flags a >8% perf regression
Profile publishing pipeline writes immutable artifacts to runtime-artifacts bucket and creates a release entry with semantic version
Rollout policy supports canary (0.5-5% traffic), automatic health checks, and immediate rollback to previous pinned profile
Onboard checklist is usable by model-owners: QC tests, memory safety checks, and a required review by Applied ML
technical_notes: Background: MoE and GQA introduce nonuniform compute patterns (expert routing stalls, grouped matmuls) which require different kernel tilings and KV cache layouts. Implementation notes: 1) Extend compile-key to include shard topology (expert_shards:x), routing strategy, and group_size to avoid cross-model cache collisions. 2) Add a small ABI header to kernel artifacts that encodes expected tensor layout and prefetch plan so runtime can assert compatibility at load-time. 3) Compile flags: use tiling=auto, split-kv-cache=true for large seqs, fused_gqa_matmul=true where group_size>1. 4) Fallbacks: when optimized kernel fails on a given GPU, fall back to a verified scalar kernel and mark the profile health degraded. 5) Quantization: record quantization profile id in manifest and ensure compile path includes dequant ops if needed. 6) Cache: include model version, profile hash, and GPU kernel version in cache key to prevent phantom cache reuse. 7) Publishing: artifacts go to s3://runtime-artifacts/compile-profiles/<model>/<profile_hash>.tar.gz with metadata JSON alongside. 8) Pinning: model manifest gets fields pinned_compile_profile and pinned_profile_timestamp; pinning is immutable except via a controlled rollout PR.
test_plan: Unit: compile-key canonicalization tests covering combinations of shard topologies, group sizes, and seq lengths
Integration: nightly compile of representative MoE/GQA models across cuda-12.1 and cuda-12.3 kernels with artifact upload to staging bucket
Perf regression: run eval harness using real prompt set (10k queries) and assert P95 latency delta <8% vs baseline
Smoke: canary rollout to a small dedicated pool and continuous health checks for 24h before wider rollout
Chaos: simulate a kernel load failure and verify automatic fallback and audit log entries
rollout_plan: Stage 0: publish profile to staging bucket and run full CI (compile + perf + mem safety)
Stage 1: canary rollout to 1% of traffic on runtime-dedicated-canary pool for 6 hours, automated P50/P95 checks
Stage 2: expand to 10% for 24 hours if health OK, run additional throughput tests
Stage 3: full rollout to pinned pool and mark profile release as GA; create rollback snapshot of previous profile
Rollback triggers: >8% P95 regression, memory OOMs, increased error rate >1% absolute
